q: In a Mealy machine, the output depends on…
options: the current state and the input symbol being read
the number of symbols read so far
explain: λ : Q × Σ → Δ. Each transition carries its own output, written input / output on the arrow.

q: A Mealy machine reads an input of length n. How long is its output?
options: It depends on the number of states
explain: One output per transition, and there is no extra output at the start, unlike a Moore machine.

q: When you convert a Moore machine to a Mealy machine, the output on the transition q —a→ p is…
options: λ(p), the output of the state entered
λ(q), the output of the state left
explain: λ′(q, a) = λ(δ(q, a)). When the Moore machine enters p, it prints p's output, so the Mealy transition prints that same symbol.

q: A Moore machine has n states. How many states does the equivalent Mealy machine built by the standard conversion have?
explain: The states and transitions are kept unchanged. Only the outputs move from the states onto the arrows.

q: A Mealy machine has n states and an output alphabet of m symbols. The equivalent Moore machine needs at most about…
explain: Each Mealy state may be split into one copy per output that enters it, which is at most m copies. Sometimes one extra start state is added.

q: The Mealy machine 'output 1 when the current symbol equals the previous one' (q₀ —0/0→ A, q₀ —1/0→ B, A —0/1→ A, A —1/0→ B, B —0/0→ A, B —1/1→ B) reads 0011. What is its output?
explain: q₀→A prints 0; A→A on 0 prints 1; A→B on 1 prints 0; B→B on 1 prints 1. So the output is 0101.

q: A Moore machine and a Mealy machine are considered equivalent if their outputs agree on every input once the Moore machine's first output symbol is ignored.
explain: True. The Moore machine's extra initial output λ(q₀) is not produced by any input, so it is left out of the comparison.

q: What is the minimum number of states in a Mealy machine that outputs the 1's complement of its binary input?
explain: One state with two self-loops, 0/1 and 1/0, is enough. Nothing needs to be remembered.

q: When converting a Mealy machine to a Moore machine, when must a state q be split?
options: When the transitions entering q carry different outputs
When q has more than two outgoing transitions
When q is the start state
explain: A Moore state has exactly one output. If q is entered with outputs 0 and 1, it needs one copy for each.

q: For the same input–output behaviour, which model typically needs fewer states?
options: They always need exactly the same number
explain: A Mealy machine can attach different outputs to different arrows from one state. A Moore machine may need several copies of a state to do the same.
